segments.title: Groundwork for EditPokemonPage
context: This change adds a page that edits a Pokemon, and an Edit link to it on the page of each Pokemon. The edit page opens the Pokemon form with the saved name, level, type and trainer, and a save writes the changes to the database and opens the page of the Pokemon again.

waypoints.title: Added the server action `updatePokemon()` to save an edited Pokemon
waypoints.reading:
The author added a server action `updatePokemon()` that:

- reads the fields of the form with [`readPokemonFields()`](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#L10-18)
- saves them on the Pokemon with the given id with [`savePokemon()`](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#savePokemon)
- calls `revalidatePath("/pokemon/3")` for the Pokemon with id 3, so that the cached page of that Pokemon is rendered again with the saved values
- redirects to `/pokemon/3`

It takes the id before the form data, so that [the edit page binds the id](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/edit/page.tsx#L15) and passes [`<PokemonForm />`](code:src/app/pokemon/components/PokemonForm.tsx#PokemonForm) a function of the form data alone, the same shape as [`createPokemon()`](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#L20-23).
waypoints.coreChange: This is where a save of the edit page reaches the database: the form data goes through the same [`readPokemonFields()`](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#L10-18) as a new Pokemon, then to [`savePokemon()`](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#savePokemon) for one id.

findings.title: `updatePokemon()` redirects as after a save when no row has the id
findings.reading: [`savePokemon()` returns `void`](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#L15), and [its update changes no row when no Pokemon has the id](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#L16). `updatePokemon()` then redirects to `/pokemon/3` as after a save, and [the Pokemon page renders the 404 page](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/page.tsx#L8). Nothing tells the professor that the edits were not saved. No code in this repository deletes a Pokemon, so only a row deleted outside the app between the load of the edit page and the save reaches this. Should the save say that the Pokemon no longer exists?

waypoints.title: Modified `PokemonFormProps` to take an optional Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author modified the interface `PokemonFormProps` to add an optional prop `pokemon` of [the type `Pokemon`](code:src/db/schema.ts#L18), a row of the `pokemon` table. [The edit page passes the Pokemon it loaded](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/edit/page.tsx#L15), and `src/app/pokemon/new/page.tsx` passes none, so that the edit page and the new Pokemon page render the same form.

waypoints.title: Modified `<PokemonForm />` to fill in a saved Pokemon
waypoints.reading:
The author modified the component `<PokemonForm />` to use the prop `pokemon` as the default value of each field:

- the name, the level and the type inputs show `pokemon.name`, `pokemon.level` and `pokemon.primaryType`
- the trainer select opens on `pokemon.trainerId`, or on `""` for `No trainer` when the Pokemon has no trainer or no Pokemon is given

[The edit page passes the Pokemon it loaded](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/edit/page.tsx#L15), so that a professor changes the saved values and does not type them again. Without a `pokemon`, as in `src/app/pokemon/new/page.tsx`, each input gets `undefined` and stays empty, and the select opens on `No trainer` as before.

waypoints.title: Added the query `savePokemon()` to update a Pokemon
waypoints.reading: The author added a query `savePokemon()` that sets the given fields on the row of the `pokemon` table with the given `id`, and returns nothing. It writes every field it gets, so a professor who picks `No trainer` sets `trainer_id` to `null`, because [`readPokemonFields()` returns `trainerId: null` for `No trainer`](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#L16). [`updatePokemon()` calls it with the fields of the form](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#L26), so that a save on the edit page changes the Pokemon in the database.

segments.title: New EditPokemonPage
context: This segment adds the edit page of a Pokemon, which loads the Pokemon and the trainers and shows the Pokemon form with the saved values. A save writes the changes to that Pokemon and opens its page, and an id that matches no Pokemon shows the 404 page.

traceDiagram.title: Load and save Pokemon flow diagram
traceDiagram.description: This diagram shows how the edit page loads a Pokemon and the trainers and renders them in the Pokemon form. It also shows what happens when the user clicks Save, and how the changed Pokemon reaches the database through [`savePokemon()`](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#savePokemon).

When a professor clicks Save, [the form calls `action` with the form data](code:src/app/pokemon/components/PokemonForm.tsx#L12).

On the edit page, `action` is `updatePokemon.bind(null, 3)`, so [`updatePokemon(3, formData)`](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#updatePokemon) runs on the server.

waypoints.title: Added `<EditPokemonPage />` to edit a Pokemon
waypoints.reading:
The author added a page component `<EditPokemonPage />` at `/pokemon/[id]/edit` that:

- loads the Pokemon of the id in the URL with [`findPokemon()`](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#L5-8), and renders the 404 page when no Pokemon has that id
- loads the trainers with [`findTrainers()`](code:src/db/queries/trainers.ts#L5-7)
- renders the heading `Edit` with the name of the Pokemon, such as `Edit Pikachu`
- renders [`<PokemonForm />`](code:src/app/pokemon/components/PokemonForm.tsx#PokemonForm) with the Pokemon, the trainers and [`updatePokemon()`](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#updatePokemon) bound to the id of the Pokemon

[The Edit link of the Pokemon page opens it](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/page.tsx#L15), so that a professor can change a Pokemon after it is created.
waypoints.coreChange: This is the page the pull request exists for: it loads a saved Pokemon into [the form of a new Pokemon](code:src/app/pokemon/components/PokemonForm.tsx#PokemonForm) and saves it through [`updatePokemon()`](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#updatePokemon). The other cards fill the form, update the row and link to this page.

children.title: Added the read of the id from the URL
children.reading: The author added a statement that awaits `params` and reads `id`, such as `"3"` for `/pokemon/3/edit`. `id` is a string, so [the next line turns it into a number](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/edit/page.tsx#L9) for [`findPokemon()`](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#L5-8).

children.title: Added the load of the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a call to [`findPokemon(3)`](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#L5-8) for `/pokemon/3/edit`, which returns the Pokemon with id 3, or `undefined` when no row has that id. [The condition below renders the 404 page for `undefined`](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/edit/page.tsx#L10).

findings.title: `<EditPokemonPage />` sends `NaN` to Postgres for an id that is not a number
findings.reading: `Number(id)` returns `NaN` for `/pokemon/abc/edit`, and [`findPokemon(NaN)` sends `NaN` as the id of the query](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#L6). The `id` column is [a `serial`](code:src/db/schema.ts#L10), so Postgres returns an error for the input `NaN`, and the page fails with a server error before [the condition below renders the 404 page](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/edit/page.tsx#L10). No database runs for this repository, so the error was not reproduced. [The Pokemon page reads its id the same way](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/page.tsx#L7).
trace: [`db.select().from(pokemon).where(eq(pokemon.id, NaN))`](code:src/db/queries/pokemon.ts#L6) → Postgres returns `invalid input syntax for type integer: "NaN"`, and the query throws.
findings.solution: const pokemon = Number.isInteger(Number(id)) ? await findPokemon(Number(id)) : undefined

children.title: Added the 404 for a Pokemon that does not exist
children.reading: The author added a condition that calls `notFound()` when `pokemon` is `undefined`. `notFound()` throws, so Next.js renders the 404 page, and the lines below run only with a Pokemon, as on [the Pokemon page](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/page.tsx#L8).

children.title: Added the load of the trainers
children.reading: The author added a call to [`findTrainers()`](code:src/db/queries/trainers.ts#L5-7), which returns every trainer ordered by name. [The form renders one option per trainer](code:src/app/pokemon/components/PokemonForm.tsx#L18-22) in its trainer select, as it does for `src/app/pokemon/new/page.tsx`.

children.title: Added the save action bound to the Pokemon
children.reading: The author added a prop `action` that holds `updatePokemon.bind(null, 3)` for the Pokemon with id 3. It is a function of the form data alone, [the type that `PokemonFormProps` gives `action`](code:src/app/pokemon/components/PokemonForm.tsx#L5). When a professor clicks Save, [the form calls it](code:src/app/pokemon/components/PokemonForm.tsx#L12), and the call reaches [`updatePokemon(3, formData)`](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#updatePokemon), so that the save updates this Pokemon and inserts no new one.

segments.title: Modified PokemonPage
context: This segment adds an Edit link under the level and the type on the page of a Pokemon, which opens the edit page of that Pokemon.

waypoints.title: Modified `<PokemonPage />` to link to the edit page
waypoints.reading: The author modified the page component `<PokemonPage />` to render a `<Link>` with the text `Edit` under the level and the type, to `/pokemon/3/edit` for the Pokemon with id 3. Next.js renders [`<EditPokemonPage />`](code:src/app/pokemon/[id]/edit/page.tsx#EditPokemonPage) at that path, so that a professor can open the edit page from the Pokemon. [`updatePokemon()` redirects back to this page after a save](code:src/app/pokemon/actions.ts#L28).
